# 1 Samuel Chapter 16 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 159r–159v | **Source Image:** 1SA_016_page_001.jpg, 1SA_016_page_002.jpg

---

**1** And the LORD said to Samuel, "How long will you mourn for Saul, seeing I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have provided for Myself a king among his sons."

**2** And Samuel said, "How can I go? If Saul hears of it, he will kill me." And the LORD said, "Take a heifer with you and say, 'I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.'

**3** And you shall call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will make known to you what you shall do, and you shall anoint for Me the one I indicate to you."

**4** And Samuel did what the LORD spoke, and he came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the city came trembling to meet him and said, "Do you come in peace?"

**5** And he said, "In peace. I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice." And he consecrated Jesse and his sons and called them to the sacrifice.

**6** And when they came, he looked upon Eliab and thought, "Surely the LORD's anointed stands before Him."

**7** But the LORD said to Samuel, "Do not look upon his appearance or the height of his stature, for I have rejected him. For the LORD does not see as man sees; man looks upon the outward appearance, but the LORD looks upon the heart."

**8** Then Jesse called Abinadab and made him pass before Samuel. And he said, "Neither has the LORD chosen this one."

**9** Then Jesse made Shammah pass by. And he said, "Neither has the LORD chosen this one."

**10** And Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel. And Samuel said to Jesse, "The LORD has not chosen these."

**11** Then Samuel said to Jesse, "Are these all the young men?" And he said, "There remains yet the youngest, and behold, he is tending the sheep." And Samuel said to Jesse, "Send for him, for we will not sit down until he comes."

**12** And he sent and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance. And the LORD said, "Arise, anoint him, for this is the one."

**13** And Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers. And the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward. Then Samuel rose and went to Ramah.

**14** Now the Spirit of the LORD had departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD tormented him.

**15** And Saul's servants said to him, "Behold, an evil spirit from God is tormenting you.

**16** Let our lord now command your servants who are before you to seek out a man who is skilled in playing the lyre. And when the evil spirit from God is upon you, he will play, and it will be well with you."

**17** And Saul said to his servants, "Find me a man who plays well and bring him to me."

**18** And one of the young men answered and said, "Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who is skilled in playing, a mighty man of valor, a man of war, prudent in speech, a man of fine appearance, and the LORD is with him."

**19** So Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, "Send me David your son, who is with the sheep."

**20** And Jesse took a donkey laden with bread, a skin of wine, and a young goat, and sent them by the hand of David his son to Saul.

**21** And David came to Saul and entered his service. And Saul loved him greatly, and David became his armor-bearer.

**22** And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, "Let David remain in my service, for he has found favor in my sight."

**23** And whenever the spirit from God was upon Saul, David would take the lyre and play it. And there would be relief for Saul, and it would be well with him, and the evil spirit would depart from him.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

1. **16:1 — "horn" (qeren)**: Samuel fills a horn with oil — not the flask (pak) used for Saul's anointing (10:1). The horn is the instrument of permanent, dynastic anointing. This is a deliberate contrast.

2. **16:7 — "the LORD looks upon the heart"**: The programmatic verse of the chapter. The verb ra'ah ("to see") appears seven times in this chapter, creating a motif of divine versus human perception. LOGOS preserves this thematic through consistent use of "look upon."

3. **16:12 — "ruddy" (admoni)**: The same adjective describes Esau (Gen 25:25). David's ruddy appearance may connect to vitality, blood, and warrior themes. The description is remarkably physical for a moment of divine selection.

4. **16:13 — "rushed upon"**: The Spirit's movement upon David is described with the verb צָלַח (tsalach), conveying sudden, forceful empowerment — the same verb used of Samson (Judg 14:6). This stands in direct contrast to the next verse, where the Spirit departs from Saul.

5. **16:14 — "an evil spirit from the LORD"**: The Hebrew is unambiguous: רוּחַ רָעָה מֵאֵת יְהוָה. LOGOS does not soften the attribution. The theology of the passage presents both the gift and the withdrawal of divine spirit as acts of sovereign will.

6. **16:18 — fivefold description**: David's introduction through a servant's report lists five qualities — skilled musician, mighty warrior, man of war, prudent in speech, handsome in form — plus the decisive sixth: "the LORD is with him." This is the most elaborate character introduction in Samuel.

— LOGOS
